# Crime Report Dataset | Practice Set - 9
## Contents Dataset Link Your Dashboard Should Include Dataset Explanation Dashboard Screenshot Submission Instructions to submit your assignment
##Dataset Link You have been given a dataset consisting of crime reports in `csv` format. Your task is to utilize your data visualization skills to create an informative and visually appealing dashboard based on this dataset. However, before creating the dashboard, you will need to perform data cleaning and utilize DAX formulas to enhance the quality of the visualizations. Click here to download the dataset ## Problem Statement The objective of this assignment is to to clean the dataset, analyze the provided columns, and design a dashboard that effectively communicates insights regarding the given crime data. Ensure that your dashboard is visually appealing, interactive, and provides valuable insights to the viewers. ## Your Dashboard Should Include 1. How many total crime reports, average age of victim,number of male victim and female victim? 2. What are the top 10 areas with the highest number of reported crimes? 3. What are the most common types of crimes reported? 4. What are the top 5 most commonly used weapons in reported crimes? 5. What are the geographic locations of the reported crimes? 6. How does the distribution of crime types vary between weekdays and weekends? 7. What is the overall trend in the number of reported crimes over time? ##Dataset Explanation **DR_NO -** This column likely represents the Report Number. **Date Rptd -** This column indicates the date when the crime was reported to the authorities. **DATE OCC -** This column represents the date on which the crime actually occurred. **AREA CODE -** This column represents the Area Code. In the context of crime reports. **AREA NAME -** This column contains the name or label of the specific area where the crime occurred. **Rpt Dist No -** This column likely refers to the Report District Number. **Crm Cd -** This column represents the Crime Code. **Crm Desc -** This column contains the description of the crime corresponding to the Crime Code. **Vict Age-** This column represents the age of the victim involved in the reported crime. **Vict Gender -** This column indicates the gender of the victim.(F - Female, M - Male, X - Unknow) **Vict Descent -** This column denotes the ethnic or racial descent of the victim. (Descent Code: A - Other Asian, B - Black, C - Chinese, D - Cambodian, F - Filipino, G - Guamanian, H - Hispanic/Latin/Mexican, I - American Indian/Alaskan Native, J - Japanese, K - Korean, L - Laotian, O - Other, P - Pacific Islander, S - Samoan, U - Hawaiian, V - Vietnamese, W - White, X - Unknown, Z - Asian Indian) **Premis Cd -** This column represents the Premises Code. It indicates the numerical code assigned to describe the type of location where the crime occurred, such as a residence, commercial establishment, or public area. **Premis Desc -** This column contains the description or name of the premises corresponding to the Premises Code. **Weapon Used Cd -** This column represents the Weapon Used Code. It denotes the numerical code assigned to describe the type of weapon, if any, used in the commission of the crime. **Weapon Desc -** This column contains the description or name of the weapon corresponding to the Weapon Used Code. **Status -** This column represents the Status of the crime report. **Status Desc -** This column contains the description or name of the status corresponding to the Status Code. **LOCATION -** This column represents the specific location or address where the crime occurred. ## Dashboard Screenshot Submission Please access the link provided below and follow the instructions to complete the submission process. Click here to submit. ## Instructions to submit your assignment 1. Take a screenshot of your completed Power BI dashboard. Press the "Windows" key, "Shift" key, and "S" key together to open the Windows Snipping Tool, which allows you to select a specific area of the screen to capture. 1. Save the screenshot. 1. Go to Google Drive and sign in with your Google account. 1. Click on the ``New`` button on the left-hand side of the screen and select ``File upload`` from the drop-down menu. 1. Select the image file you want to upload and click "Open." The file will be uploaded to your Google Drive. 1. Once the file has finished uploading, go to ``Recent`` to find your uploaded image. 1. Right-click on the image file and select "Share" from the drop-down menu. 1. In the "General access" section, click on the drop-down and select "Anyone with the link". 1. Click on the "Copy link" button to copy the link to the image file and then click on ``Done`` button. 1. Open Submit form by clicking ``Click here to submit`` and enter your Name, User ID will be filled automatically don't change it. 1. Paste the link of your Dashboard screenshot which you have copied from Google Drive. 1. Submit the form.

# IPL Dataset - Practice Set 10
## Contents Dataset Link Your Dashboard Should Include Dataset Explanation Dashboard Screenshot Submission Instructions to submit your assignment
##Dataset Link You have been given an IPL dataset in `CSV` format. Your task is to utilize your data visualization skills to create an informative and visually appealing dashboard based on this dataset. However, before creating the dashboard, you will need to perform data cleaning and utilize DAX formulas to enhance the quality of the visualizations. Click here to download the dataset ## Problem Statement As an aspiring data analyst, you have been given access to an IPL dataset containing information about matches played from 2008 to 2016. Your task is to create an interactive and visually appealing dashboard that provides valuable insights and answers to the following questions: ## Your Dashboard Should Include 1. How many IPL matches were played each season? 2. Which team has won the most matches overall? 3. Which four cities hosted the most IPL matches? 4. Which player has won the most "player of the Match" awards? 5. How many matches were affected by the "Duckworth-Lewis" method? 6. How many matches were won by each team in each venue? 7. Which five venues hosted the most IPL matches? ##Dataset Explanation **City -** The name of the city where the IPL match was held. **Date -** The date on which the IPL match took place. **Dl_applied -** This column indicates the Duckworth-Lewis method during the match. '0' means not applied, and '1' means applied. **ID -** A unique identifier for each match in the dataset. **Player of match -** The name of the player who was awarded the "Man of the Match" for their outstanding performance in the match. **Result -** The result of the match. **Season -** The year or season in which the IPL match was played. **Team1 -** The name of one of the teams participating in the match. **Team2 -** The name of the other team participating in the match. **Toss_decision -** The decision made by the team winning the toss, whether to bat or field first. **Toss_winner -** The name of the team that won the coin toss before the match. **Umpire1 -** The name of the first on-field umpire for the match. **Umpire2 -** The name of the second on-field umpire for the match. **Umpire3 -** In some cases, there is a third umpire involved, and this column would contain their name. **Venue -** The name of the stadium or venue where the IPL match was held. **Win by runs -** If the team batting first won the match, this column would contain the number of runs by which they won. **Win by wickets -** If the team batting second won the match, this column would contain the number of wickets remaining when they achieved victory. **Winner -** The name of the team that won the match. ## Dashboard Screenshot Submission Please access the link provided below and follow the instructions to complete the submission process. Click here to submit. ## Instructions to submit your assignment 1. Take a screenshot of your completed Power BI dashboard. Press the "Windows" key, "Shift" key, and "S" key together to open the Windows Snipping Tool, which allows you to select a specific area of the screen to capture. 1. Save the screenshot. 1. Go to Google Drive and sign in with your Google account. 1. Click on the ``New`` button on the left-hand side of the screen and select ``File upload`` from the drop-down menu. 1. Select the image file you want to upload and click "Open." The file will be uploaded to your Google Drive. 1. Once the file has finished uploading, go to ``Recent`` to find your uploaded image. 1. Right-click on the image file and select "Share" from the drop-down menu. 1. In the "General access" section, click on the drop-down and select "Anyone with the link". 1. Click on the "Copy link" button to copy the link to the image file and then click on ``Done`` button. 1. Open Submit form by clicking ``Click here to submit`` and enter your Name, User ID will be filled automatically don't change it. 1. Paste the link of your Dashboard screenshot which you have copied from Google Drive. 1. Submit the form.
